feature: Feasibility spike: script-based evidence tier tagging
problem: risk_policy.evaluate_risk() currently infers hypothesis tiers (SUPPORTED/SPECULATIVE) from unstructured LLM reasoning text. Before building evidence_tagger.py in iter-3b, we need to know if a script can match evidence quotes to diff hunks with ≥80% tier agreement vs LLM labels — or if a hybrid/blocked approach is required.
proposed_solution: Build scripts/spike_evidence_tagger.py: parse STAGE 3 blocks from reasoning_summary, extract evidence_quote per hypothesis, test quote presence against truncated diff (matching the 16K cap the LLM saw), compare script tier to LLM tier. Curate ≥12 panel fixtures. Report decision: pure_script | hybrid | blocked.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Fixture corpus at tests/fixtures/evidence_tagger_panel.json with ≥12 entries, each having {commit_id, hypothesis_id, evidence_quote, expected_tier, curation}
AC-2: prototype tag_hypothesis() achieves ≥80% strict 4-way tier agreement across the corpus
AC-3: Decision documented in spike report: pure_script | hybrid | blocked, with quantitative evidence (strict_agreement, binary_supported_agreement, supported_quote_extraction_rate)
AC-4: Spike report at .harness/evals/spike-evidence-tagger.json with schema {task_id, decision, metrics, failures, recommendation_for_iter_3b}
edge_cases: EC-1: Truncated diff — fbf0ff H2 and 9530370 H3 are UNVERIFIABLE because diff is truncated; script must not tag these SUPPORTED when quote is beyond truncation marker
EC-2: 572f3cee has no defect hypotheses (STAGE 3: N/A); corpus must still include ≥1 row from this commit or document the gap
verification_method: Run: .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_evidence_tagger_spike.py -q (AC-2 assertion strict_agreement>=0.80); python scripts/spike_evidence_tagger.py --evaluate (produces report); cat .harness/evals/spike-evidence-tagger.json | python3 -m json.tool (validates schema)
